name: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex

criteria.description: Recurrent skin blistering localized to areas of mechanical trauma
Intraepidermal cleavage within basal keratinocytes on skin biopsy
Identification of pathogenic variants in KRT5 or KRT14 genes
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical blistering plus either histopathological confirmation or pathogenic genetic variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is confirmatory and helps subtype classification.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Blistering localized to basal keratinocyte layer

common.symptomName: Erosions and crusting following blister rupture
Pain and tenderness at blister sites

occasional.symptomName: Heat intolerance due to impaired skin barrier

rare.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic skin loss

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing intraepidermal cleavage at basal keratinocyte level
Immunofluorescence mapping demonstrating keratin 5 and 14 abnormalities
other: Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Blistering occurs within lamina lucida of basement membrane
Scarring and nail loss more prominent

redFlags: Extensive mucosal involvement causing feeding difficulties
Signs of secondary infection with systemic symptoms
Rapidly progressive blistering with systemic illness
references: Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2014.
Uitto J, et al. Molecular genetics of epidermolysis bullosa simplex. Exp Dermatol. 2016.
Orphanet: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex. Available at: https://www.orpha.net
